elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The Customer carve-out expressly permits assignment “without consent, to an affiliate.”

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The Customer carve-out expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor organization by merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The Customer carve-out expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor organization by acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets.
elements.evidence: The Customer carve-out expressly covers a successor organization resulting from a sale of substantially all of Customer’s assets.

elements.element: IBM may not assign this Agreement without Customer's prior consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence makes assignment subject to the other party’s prior written consent, so IBM must obtain Customer’s consent.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to an IBM assignment.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent requirement states that consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: IBM may never assign this Agreement to a competitor of Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause separately and categorically states that “IBM will not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Customer,” so Customer consent would not override the prohibition.

elements.element: IBM has no right to terminate this Agreement upon a change of control of Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants IBM no termination right or other remedy triggered by Customer’s change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign without consent to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The Customer successor carve-out contains no written-notice requirement.

elements.element: IBM may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: No successor carve-out applies to IBM; every IBM assignment remains subject to Customer’s prior written consent.

elements.element: IBM must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no written-notice mechanism for an IBM successor assignment.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than assignments to a successor require IBM's prior written consent.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent even when the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: IBM may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Customer assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent provision expressly states that consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: IBM assignments other than assignments to a successor require Customer's prior written consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires Customer’s prior written consent for every IBM assignment, including non-successor assignments.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to an IBM assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent provision expressly states that consent may not be unreasonably withheld, although IBM remains absolutely prohibited from assigning to a Customer competitor.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred position: Customer receives the specified affiliate and successor carve-outs, IBM assignments require Customer consent subject to a reasonableness standard, competitor assignments are absolutely prohibited, and no Customer change-of-control termination right is created. The fallback is not fully satisfied because neither party has the required written-notice framework and IBM lacks a consent-free successor-assignment right. The changes are confined to the assignment allocation and preserve the existing void-assignment and Customer-liability provisions.
